content.title: About
content.content: Jam (or jelly) is a sweet spread made by cooking fruit, berries or vegetables with sugar and sometimes pectin. It is commonly used as a topping for toast, pastries, desserts and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “jam” usually refers to a product that contains fruit pieces, while “jelly” denotes a smoother, gel‑like consistency.
Pectin, a natural thickener, is found in the skins and seeds of many fruits, especially apples and citrus.
In the United States jams are classified by sugar content: regular, low‑sugar and no‑sugar‑added.
Traditional English jam is often made from raspberries, strawberries or blackcurrants.
In some countries (e.g., Japan) jelly is made with agar‑agar instead of pectin.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Fruit jams retain some vitamin C, which supports immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber in jam with fruit pieces aids digestion.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar provides a quick source of energy, making jam a convenient light snack.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit components (berries, cherries, apricots) contain polyphenols that may reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Enhances flavor of dishes
items.content: Jam and jelly add sweetness and aroma without needing large amounts of fresh fruit.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Most jam consists of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: People allergic to certain fruits (e.g., strawberries) may react even after cooking.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial varieties contain artificial preservatives and flavorings that may cause sensitivities.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of jam can irritate the stomach lining in individuals with gastritis or reflux.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Jam can be spread on bread, rolls, pancakes, used as a filling for cupcakes, pies and cheesecakes. Jelly is often served as a sauce for ice cream, cottage cheese or as a light dessert on its own.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store jam or jelly in a tightly sealed glass jar in the refrigerator after opening. When kept in a cool, dark place unopened, it can last up to 12 months. Discard if the product develops off‑odors, color changes or mold.
